reviews.text: [h1]Experienced on the Meta Quest 3[/h1] You can view my gameplay & early impressions here: https://youtu.be/CK7nelZwg28 This is a budget-priced sailing game for VR, so keep your expectations in check. I wouldn't compare it to VR Regatta because they are in different leagues both in quality and in price. Obviously, VR Regatta is the much better game, but this game is alright for the budget price. My biggest complaint is that during the race competition my sail boat would be knocked off course, like in a collision, but without seeing what hit me. This only happened once though, so hopefully it's a rare bug. The other big complaint is the controls. They're not very immersive. You basically hold the rudder with your left trigger and a bead on a rope with the right trigger for moving the sails. The controls are just too basic and they really bring down the immersion for this game. The visuals are okay for this budget price. The sounds are pretty much just the ocean wave sounds, which was disappointing. The gameplay is nice, but the sail boat colliding really brought it down. I don't want to sound too negative though, because I was enjoying the game for the most part. It's just that the negatives are pretty difficult to ignore. However, I think the game is overall fine for this budget price. [b]Rate 5.5/10.[/b] [quote]Please note: I received a free Steam key through the Steam Curator Connect program. If you enjoyed my review, please consider joining my Steam Curator group [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/Oculus_WMR]Oculus Rift Reviews.[/url][/quote]

When watching the movie Ocean Romance, I really wanted to be able to bravely sail a small boat like Moana to various corners of the world according to my own wishes. After learning about this software, I immediately started it. Sailing on the sea is really interesting. The wind direction on the sea is constantly changing, sometimes with the wind, sometimes against the wind, and sometimes with the wind. But don't be afraid, adjust the sail according to the wind direction at any time and set sail towards your destination.

What's in the ocean? Is there a mermaid? Are there any extraterrestrial creatures? I really want to swim in the ocean! Carrying a series of surprises, the sail sailed out to sea, and the person rushing to the sea started walking.

I am increasingly fond of being alone and enjoying sailing with a friend, but now the cost is huge. This software is affordable and allows unlimited access to various bays for competitions and Taobao. It's fun!

Driving a sailboat out to sea requires constant vigilance. The sailboat dances with the waves, with ups and downs, and even a slight mistake can lead to capsizing right in front of us. It can be said that every fluctuation of the waves is a test of courage and perseverance, and also a way to communicate with the sea.
The gate remains closed, the two gates remain closed, yet they conquer the seas of various places and set sail.

The sea embraces all rivers, and tolerance is great. At a glance, the sea and sky merge into one color. Riding a sailboat and immersing oneself in it, one can feel its inclusive power and instantly broaden one's mind.
Rowing a boat into the sea, driving a sailboat, with the ups and downs of the waves and changes in wind direction, the sailboat also rises and falls, bouncing and swaying.
The sea in this software is too real, with waves, sea breeze, seabirds, and more, and sailboats rising and falling with the ups and downs of the waves.

So the waves can be chosen! At first, I felt that the waves were very strong and the small sailboat could capsize at any time. Later, after careful searching, I found out that there were three levels of waves.
С волнами и морским бризом, плывущим вдаль, было очень приятно.
海が好きで、このゲームの中で舟を浮かべて海を渡る感じが好きで、風波の起伏に従って、ゆらゆらと世界各地の有名な湾に行きます。

VR Sailing by HFRK. is a focused virtual reality experience built around a single idea: placing the player on open water and letting them control a sailboat through direct interaction. It does not attempt to follow the structure of a traditional game, and instead positions itself as a simulation-lite sandbox where immersion and physical engagement take priority over progression or narrative. From the moment you step into the environment, it becomes clear that the experience is designed to be slow, deliberate, and centered on the sensation of movement rather than on objectives or challenge. The core mechanic revolves around steering and adjusting a sailboat using VR controls, with an emphasis on mimicking the feel of real sailing in a simplified form. Players must consider wind direction, positioning, and the angle of their sails to maintain movement, creating a rhythm that is more about subtle adjustment than constant input. When the system aligns properly, it can produce moments of convincing immersion, where the act of turning the boat or catching the wind feels natural within the virtual space. These moments are where the game is at its strongest, capturing a sense of calm and presence that is difficult to replicate outside of VR. However, the simulation itself is relatively shallow. While the game introduces basic elements of sailing mechanics, it does not fully explore the complexity of real-world systems. Controls can feel imprecise, and the feedback between player actions and the boat’s response is not always consistent. This inconsistency can break immersion, particularly for players expecting a more accurate or detailed simulation. As a result, the experience sits somewhere between a realistic interpretation and a simplified representation, without fully committing to either approach. The environments are designed to support the feeling of openness rather than to provide interactive depth. Expanses of water, distant landforms, and minimal environmental detail create a sense of scale, especially when viewed in VR. The lack of clutter helps maintain clarity and reinforces the calm tone of the experience, but it also contributes to a sense of emptiness. There is little in the way of dynamic events, environmental hazards, or meaningful interaction beyond the act of sailing itself. Over time, this lack of variety can make the world feel static, reducing the sense of discovery. Structurally, the game offers almost no traditional progression. There are no missions, objectives, or narrative elements guiding the player forward. Instead, the experience is entirely self-directed, allowing players to explore and experiment at their own pace. This open-ended design can be appealing for those who want a relaxed, meditative experience, as it removes pressure and allows for uninterrupted immersion. At the same time, it can also make the game feel aimless, particularly once the initial novelty of controlling the boat wears off. Audio design plays a supporting role in maintaining immersion. Ambient sounds such as wind and water movement reinforce the sensation of being at sea, adding subtle depth to the experience. The audio is understated and does not attempt to dominate the atmosphere, which aligns well with the game’s calm and minimalistic tone. While it is effective in its role, it does not introduce significant variety or standout moments. Accessibility is one of the game’s more notable strengths. The controls are relatively easy to understand, and the lack of complex systems makes it approachable even for players who are new to VR or simulation experiences. This simplicity allows players to quickly engage with the core mechanic without needing extensive tutorials or prior knowledge. However, this same simplicity also limits the depth of the experience, as there are few additional layers to explore once the basics are mastered. Replayability is largely dependent on how much the player enjoys the act of sailing itself. Without evolving systems, unlockable content, or structured challenges, the game relies entirely on its core mechanic to sustain interest. For some players, particularly those who enjoy calm, exploratory VR experiences, this can be enough to justify occasional returns. For others, the lack of progression and variety may lead to a short-lived engagement. Ultimately, VR Sailing is defined by its narrow scope and clear focus. It succeeds in delivering a basic, accessible interpretation of sailing within a virtual environment, capturing moments of immersion that highlight the potential of VR as a medium. At the same time, its limited depth, inconsistent mechanics, and absence of structured content prevent it from feeling like a fully developed simulation or game. For players seeking a relaxing, low-pressure VR experience centered on movement and atmosphere, it offers a simple and occasionally satisfying escape. For those looking for a deeper simulation, more refined controls, or a sense of progression and purpose, it may feel too limited. It stands as a focused experiment in immersive design, delivering on its core idea while remaining constrained by its simplicity. Rating: 7/10
